# Analyze structural complexity of each component
test_input = """9 9 9 0 3 3 9 9 9 0 9 0 0 9 9 9 9 9 9
6 6 9 3 3 3 9 9 9 0 0 0 0 9 9 9 9 9 9
6 9 9 9 9 9 9 9 9 9 9 9 9 9 9 9 2 9 9
9 9 4 4 4 9 9 9 9 9 9 9 9 9 9 2 2 9 9
9 9 4 4 4 4 9 9 9 9 1 9 9 2 2 2 9 9 9
9 9 9 9 9 9 9 1 1 1 9 9 9 2 2 9 9 9 2
9 9 9 9 9 9 1 9 1 1 1 9 9 9 2 2 2 2 9
9 9 9 9 9 9 9 9 1 1 1 9 9 9 9 9 9 9 9
9 9 9 9 0 0 0 9 9 9 9 9 9 9 9 9 4 9 9
9 9 0 0 0 0 0 9 9 9 9 9 9 9 4 4 9 9 9
9 9 9 9 9 9 9 9 9 9 7 9 9 9 9 9 9 9 9
9 9 9 6 9 9 9 2 2 9 7 9 9 9 9 9 9 4 9
9 9 9 6 9 9 9 9 2 9 7 7 9 9 9 9 9 4 9
9 9 9 6 9 9 9 9 9 9 9 7 9 9 9 9 9 9 4""".split('\n')

background = 9
from collections import defaultdict

rows, cols = len(test_input), len(test_input[0].split())
visited = set()
directions = [(0,1),(0,-1),(1,0),(-1,0)]
comp_list = []

for r in range(rows):
    for c in range(cols):
        val = int(test_input[r].split()[c])
        if val == background or (r,c) in visited:
            continue
        comp = []
        stack = [(r,c)]
        while stack:
            cr, cc = stack.pop()
            if (cr, cc) in visited:
                continue
            visited.add((cr, cc))
            comp.append((cr, cc))
            for dr, dc in directions:
                nr, nc = cr + dr, cc + dc
                if 0 <= nr < rows and 0 <= nc < cols:
                    nval = int(test_input[nr].split()[nc])
                    if nval == val and (nr, nc) not in visited:
                        stack.append((nr, nc))
        comp_list.append({'color': val, 'positions': comp})

print("All connected components:")
for i, comp in enumerate(comp_list):
    rs = min(p[0] for p in comp['positions'])
    re = max(p[0] for p in comp['positions'])
    cs = min(p[1] for p in comp['positions'])
    ce = max(p[1] for p in comp['positions'])
    vsize = re - rs + 1
    hsize = ce - cs + 1
    
    # Calculate "interestingness" - cells that touch other colors
    interesting_count = 0
    for pos in comp['positions']:
        neighbors = [(pos[0]+dr, pos[1]+dc) for dr, dc in directions]
        for npos in neighbors:
            if 0 <= npos[0] < rows and 0 <= npos[1] < cols:
                nval = int(test_input[npos[0]].split()[npos[1]])
                if nval != background and nval != comp['color']:
                    interesting_count += 1
                    break
    
    ratio = interesting_count / len(comp['positions']) if comp['positions'] else 0
    
    print(f"\nComp {i}: color={comp['color']}, bbox={vsize}x{hsize}, cells={len(comp['positions'])}")
    print(f"  Interesting ratio: {ratio:.2f}, interesting count: {interesting_count}")
